answer: Each key's actions leave a timeline: when it submits, mines, grades, idles, restarts. The network passes those timelines through a prism, splitting them into rhythms, and cross-correlates every pair over weeks. Keys run by one operator share hidden plumbing, like karst under a desert: the same crash minutes, the same rate-limit pauses, the same oasis of bursts after each deploy. Keys whose rhythms line up far beyond chance are merged into one reward slot, so a farm of extra keys earns nothing extra.
